Ⅰ.느헤미야 개관\n- 느헤미야라는 말은 나함 야훼, 여호와는 위로하신다:
Ⅰ. Nehemiah Overview
- The name Nehemiah is Nacham Yahweh, meaning 'the LORD comforts'.
<느1:1~3> 하가랴의 아들 느헤미야의 말이라 아닥사스다 왕 제 이십:
<Neh 1:1~3> The words of Nehemiah the son of Hachaliah. And it came to pass in the month Chisleu, in the twentieth year of King Artaxerxes, as I was in Shushan the palace (the Persian emperor's winter palace), That Hanani, one of my brethren, came, he and certain men (1,800 people) of Judah; and I asked them concerning the Jews that had escaped, which were left of the captivity, and concerning Jerusalem (the hardships they went through after sending away the foreign women). And they said unto me, The remnant that are left of the captivity there in the province are in great affliction and reproach: the wall of Jerusalem also is broken down, and the gates thereof are burned with fire. And it came to pass, when I heard these words, that I sat down and wept, and mourned certain days, and fasted, and prayed before the God of heaven,
 - When Nehemiah heard that news, he sat down and wept, mourned for days, and fasted before the God of heaven, and Nehemiah too was someone who had never even been to Jerusalem. From this picture of Nehemiah we can get a glimpse of how thoroughly elders like Hachaliah had given the second generation in Babylon a national education all that time.
 - Nehemiah was the Persian emperor's chief cupbearer, not just the emperor's conversation partner but one of his closest aides. Beyond the high position, he was the person the emperor trusted most. His position alone would have been plenty of excuse, but giving up all his privileges and going to a desolate frontier is truly amazing.
<느2:1~3> 아닥사스다 왕 이십년 니산월에 왕의 앞에 술이 있기로 내: <Neh 2:1~3> And it came to pass in the month Nisan, in the twentieth year of Artaxerxes the king, that wine was before him: and I took up the wine, and gave it unto the king. Now I had not been beforetime sad in his presence. Wherefore the king said unto me, Why is thy countenance sad, seeing thou art not sick? this is nothing else but sorrow of heart. Then I was very sore afraid, and said unto the king, (With a chief cupbearer, even a hint of worry on his face can get him killed. This is a man who could kill the emperor at any time. In a situation where he's under that kind of suspicion, imagine suddenly saying he's going to Jerusalem.  He'd immediately be suspected of rebellion. ) Let the king live for ever: why should not my countenance be sad, when the city, the place of my fathers' sepulchres, lieth waste, and the gates thereof are consumed with fire?
느헤미야는 재치있게 예루살렘이라고 하지 않고 조상의 묘실 있는 성읍이 불: Nehemiah cleverly doesn't say Jerusalem; he says the city where his ancestors' tombs are has been burned.
<느2:4> 왕이 내게 이르시되 그러면 네가 무엇을 원하느냐 하시기로 내:
<Neh 2:4> Then the king said unto me, For what dost thou make request? So I prayed to the God of heaven.
 - In that situation, even though the king is asking him, he doesn't answer right away; he prays silently and carefully prepares his answer. Even in that short moment.
<느2:5~6> 왕에게 고하되 왕이 만일 즐겨하시고 종이 왕의 목전에서:
<Neh 2:5~6> And I said unto the king, If it please the king, and if thy servant have found favour in thy sight, that thou wouldest send me unto Judah, unto the city of my fathers' sepulchres, that I may build it. And the king said unto me, (the queen also sitting by him,) For how long shall thy journey be? and when wilt thou return? So it pleased the king to send me; and I set him a time.
 - That time was 12 years. With the queen beside him, the emperor couldn't be stingy.
<느2:7~8> 내가 또 왕에게 아뢰되 왕이 만일 즐겨하시거든 강 서편: <Neh 2:7~8> Moreover I said unto the king, If it please the king, let letters be given me to the governors beyond the river, that they may convey me over till I come into Judah; And a letter unto Asaph the keeper of the king's forest, that he may give me timber to make beams for the gates of the palace which appertained to the house, and for the wall of the city, and for the house that I shall enter into. And the king granted me, according to the good hand of my God upon me.
또 하나님의 선한 손이 도우심으로... 또 기회를 봐서 이것 저것 요구하: And again, according to the good hand of God... he watches for his chance and asks for this and that, and the king grants it all. Sounds just like Ezra, doesn't it?
<느2:9~10> 군대 장관과 마병을 보내어 나와 함께 하게 하시기로 내: <Neh 2:9~10> Then I came to the governors beyond the river, and gave them the king's letters. Now the king had sent captains of the army and horsemen with me. When Sanballat the Horonite, and Tobiah the servant, the Ammonite, heard of it, it grieved them exceedingly that there was come a man to seek the welfare of the children of Israel.
개혁을 단행하다가 큰 난관에 봉착했던 에스라로서는 막강한 자금과 호위병,: For Ezra, who had run into great difficulties while pushing through reforms, meeting Nehemiah, who had come a long way with huge funds, a guard, and even soldiers, must have been a really great comfort. He was truly a 'Nehemiah'. The LORD helps.
<느2:11~12> 먼길을 왔는데 여독도 풀리지 않았을 때 밤에 현장을:
<Neh 2:11~12>  He'd come a long way, and before he'd even recovered from the journey, he inspected the site at night. As soon as he arrived he ran straight to the work site to find out what had happened. And no wonder, since he had never seen it once.
 - In chapter 5, the poor people are really struggling because they also have to rebuild the wall.
어떤 사람은 자기 밭이나 포도원, 심지어 자기 자녀까지 저당 잡혀서 간신:
Some people barely survived by mortgaging their fields or vineyards, even their own children, while at a time like this the rich were taking fields and vineyards as collateral and lending at interest, and as soon as the repayment date passed they did the evil thing of seizing them.
 - So Nehemiah taught Leviticus 25: you don't take interest from your brothers,
종으로 팔렸어도 종처럼 대하지 말아라. 빼앗은 거 다 돌려 줘라, 했더니:
even if he's been sold as a slave, don't treat him like a slave. Give back everything you took. And the people said they would do so.
 - And then, because Nehemiah knew how hard it was for the people, though he was governor he didn't take a salary.
 - He records that the ones before him all, without exception, took from the people and oppressed them, but because he feared God he didn't do that. Instead he did the work spending his own money.
6장에 보면 느헤미야가 살해 위협을 당하기도 합니다. 산발랏과 도비야,: In chapter 6 Nehemiah even faces death threats. Sanballat and Tobiah, Geshem the Arabian and the rest of the riffraff.  "Let's meet in one of the villages in the plain of Ono. But come alone." They mean to kill him.
느헤미야가 안 나감, 그러니까 모함을 함 ‘너 왕 되고 싶어서 그러는거: Nehemiah doesn't go,  so they slander him: 'You're doing this because you want to be king, aren't you? Honestly, there's no reason for you to work that hard, is there?'
한번은 스마야라는 사람이 정보를 줍니다. 지금 사람들이 너를 죽이려고 하: Once a man named Shemaiah gives him a tip. People are trying to kill you right now, so hurry and hide inside the temple. But later it turned out he wasn't sent by God; he was a double agent sent by Sanballat and Tobiah.
이 일에 노야다라는 사람이 끼었는데 여선지자 : 선지자 조차도 돈에 눈이: A woman named Noadiah was involved in this too, a prophetess : an age when even the prophets were blinded by money.
그야말로 목숨이 왔다 갔다 하는 상황임에도 꿋꿋하게 일을 하 나가는 느헤: Nehemiah, steadfastly pressing on with the work even in a situation where his life hung in the balance. A truly courageous man.
Now in chapter 8 they hold the first public reading of the law.
<느8:1~4> 이스라엘 자손이 그 본성에 거하였더니 칠월에 이르러는 모:
<Neh 8:1~4> and the children of Israel were in their cities. And all the people gathered themselves together as one man into the street that was before the water gate; and they spake unto Ezra the scribe to bring the book of the law of Moses, which the LORD had commanded to Israel. And Ezra the priest brought the law before the congregation both of men and women, and all that could hear with understanding, upon the first day of the seventh month. And he read therein before the street that was before the water gate from the morning until midday, before the men and the women, and those that could understand; and the ears of all the people were attentive unto the book of the law — that's what it says, right?
  - When they did this, the people realized their sin and repented, and also rejoiced and were glad in the LORD.
 - In chapter 10 they make a pledge to keep the law, and 84 people sign it. Not only that, they even swear with a curse.
3. We will keep the Sabbath year.
4. We will set ordinances and take care of the temple.
5. We will offer the sacrifices properly.
6. We will offer the firstfruits properly.
7. We will offer the firstborn and the redemption money.
8. We will give the tithe properly.
It's by reading that they come to understand.
5. 느헤미야의 재개혁과 말라기 시대의 도래\n - 느헤미야가 12년 말:
5. Nehemiah's second reform and the coming of the age of Malachi
 - Nehemiah had been given 12 years of leave, so knowing his character, when the 12 years were up he probably went back to Persia.
 - But Nehemiah went and then came back again. Because the work wasn't all finished yet.
 - So going and coming took 8 months, plus the 3~4 months he stayed, so he came back after about a year, and terrible things were going on.
 - When he came back it was a mess. What you'd call faith that depends on people. A state where people pretend when the leader is there and it all falls apart when he's gone.
 1) That guy Tobiah, who had kept threatening, intimidating, scheming and slandering, had cleared out a room in the temple, set up an office, and was sitting there.
 2) Since there were no tithes, the Levites had scattered here and there looking for a way to make a living.
 3) Men of Tyre were coming in on the Sabbath and selling goods.
 4) They had again taken foreign women as wives.
 5) One of the high priest's family had become Sanballat's son-in-law.
 - Nehemiah reforms this situation in Jerusalem once again and makes the people swear, but Nehemiah can't live forever.
결국 에스라, 느헤미야가 죽고 나니까 이스라엘 사람들의 신앙이라는 것은: In the end, once Ezra and Nehemiah died, the faith of the people of Israel became a mess, and after the Babylonian Exile they did know about God and did carry out religious practices, but they fell into formalism, and the age of Malachi arrived.
